subject: Private deployment: operator access, subprocessors, and cross-border controls
messages:
From: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@medixhealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com, legal@medixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment privacy questions and subprocessors inventory

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the product overview last week — Medix is keen to move forward with a private deployment for our PII-heavy workflows. Before procurement and legal can sign off we need clarity on a few privacy and control points so we can finalize our DPA annex. Please see the attached questionnaire (Medix_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf) and confirm the following at a high level:

- If we elect customer-managed keys (customer KMS / BYOK) will Redwood personnel ever be able to access plaintext inference data or model inputs/outputs?
- Do you maintain an operator "breakglass" process that could allow temporary elevated access? If yes, what controls and audit evidence are provided?
- Please provide a current list of subprocessors and whether any have the ability to access decrypted data.
- Any cross-border flow of customer data we should be aware of for export control or EU/UK data transfer purposes?

We would like a draft DPA annex and subprocessors inventory (CSV is fine). Procurement is pushing for explicit export-control language and a short statement that Redwood will not escrow our keys or require key escrow by default.

Can you get a response by EOD Thursday? If it's useful we can schedule a 30-min legal alignment call.

Thanks,
Sara Hayes
VP, Data & Privacy | Medix Health
+sara.hayes@medixhealth.com

Attachment: Medix_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@medixhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment privacy questions and subprocessors inventory

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (AE), Rishi (Legal/Security), and Kimberly (Infosec) so we can provide a consolidated response and the requested artifacts. Quick summary for procurement while we assemble the docs:

- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): supported. When BYOK is enabled, Redwood does not hold the plaintext encryption keys in our control plane; by default we do not have access to unencrypted inference payloads.
- Breakglass / operator access: we have an emergency operator process (used extremely rarely) — it requires multi-person approval, justification, and is fully audited. Rishi/Kimberly will propose acceptable wording for the DPA annex.
- Subprocessors: we'll attach a current inventory (Subprocessors_Inventory_202605.csv). None of the subprocessors are granted access to plaintext in BYOK configurations per our current controls.
- Cross-border transfers: default hosted telemetry and control plane endpoints are region-aware; for private deployments we can lock control-plane telecom to the customer's chosen region and add an export-control clause.

Attachments I will send shortly: Redwood_PrivDep_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf (draft), Subprocessors_Inventory_202605.csv. We will not require key escrow as a standard practice; if a customer requests escrow we treat that as a negotiated exception with contract language and technical controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi/Kimberly to provide redline suggestions for the DPA annex and suggested operator/escrow wording.
2) We will provide the subprocessors CSV and an export-control affirmation.
3) Optional legal alignment call (we can do Thu or Fri).

Alex Martinez
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Alex's mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_PrivDep_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment privacy questions and subprocessors inventory

Team — drafting notes and redline suggestions for the annex. Key points to include for Medix: 

- Operator access: add an explicit clause that, for BYOK configurations, Redwood personnel will not have access to customer plaintext or model inputs/outputs except under documented emergency breakglass. The breakglass clause should require (a) two-person approval from separate roles, (b) real-time notification to a named customer contact, and (c) write-once audit record delivered to customer within 72 hours.

- Subprocessors: include commitment to provide a 30-day notice for additions and an ability for Medix to object to specific subprocessors for reasonable cause. For the CSV we will flag any subprocessor with access rights (none currently for BYOK).

- Export/control transfers: add a clause that we will not transfer customer-controlled plaintext outside the customer's agreed geography without prior written consent. Telemetry: propose limiting logs sent to Redwood control plane to anonymized/aggregated metrics (latency, errors, token counts). Any request for raw logs must be accompanied by proof-of-legal requirement and will only be provided in encrypted form or under customer-approved access window.

Redline snippet (to go in annex):
"For Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK), Redwood will not access or retain Customer Plaintext Data. Operator access is restricted to emergency breakglass events as described in Section X.1; all breakglass activations shall be documented and delivered to Customer within seventy-two (72) hours. Redwood shall not export or transfer Customer Plaintext Data outside the geographic region specified in the Order Form without Customer's prior written consent."

I also recommend we produce a short addendum specific to export control (Export_Control_Compliance_Form.pdf) for procurement to sign. Kimberly — can you confirm the telemetry controls and what will remain in the control plane?

-Rishi

Legal Counsel (Security Reviews) | Redwood Inference

On Wed, 20 May 2026 at 08:50, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Alex/Rishi — telemetry summary: for private VPC/on-prem deployments we ship only aggregated metrics and interaction-level hashes (no plaintext). Control-plane traces include request IDs and timing; payloads are not recorded in plaintext. We will document retention windows and provide an export of audit records on request.
>
> Attachment: Export_Control_Compliance_Form.pdf (application/pdf)

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@medixhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurement@medixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment privacy questions and subprocessors inventory

Sara — appreciate the patience. Summary and attachments (see files): Redwood_PrivDep_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf, Subprocessors_Inventory_202605.csv, Export_Control_Compliance_Form.pdf. Key confirmations below: 

- No operator plaintext access with BYOK: When Medix enables customer-managed keys, Redwood does not possess the plaintext keys and therefore cannot read inference inputs/outputs.
- Breakglass: we support a documented, auditable breakglass workflow (two-person approval, documented justification, notification to customer contact). We will include the breakglass clause and audit delivery timelines in the annex.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and notes access levels. For BYOK deployments none of the subprocessors have decryption capability. We will provide 30-day notice for subprocessor additions and allow Medix to raise objections for reasonable cause.
- Cross-border / export control: we will not transfer customer-controlled plaintext outside the ordered geography without prior written consent. See Export_Control_Compliance_Form.pdf for standard language.

Proposed next step: if this lane looks acceptable, Marissa and I can coordinate a 30-min legal/procurement call next week to walk through the annex and sign-off path. Please confirm availability (we have Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_PrivDep_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf (application/pdf), Subprocessors_Inventory_202605.csv (text/csv), Export_Control_Compliance_Form.pdf (application/pdf)
